rv.q: I left the show with the feeling the playwright's work is always capable of delivering in good hands: buzzy, wide awake, like my brain had been washed in seltzer.
His production, like the play, is an impressive achievement.
You don't have to be a Classics major to fall under the magical spell of The Invention of Love.
Direction (Anothony Elkind) makes brilliant use of the space creating movement and variation that never seems extraneous.

This is one of those maddening theatrical evenings in which I admired virtually everyone responsible for putting the play onstage while desperately wishing someone had been permitted to take a red pencil to the playwright.

cn.t: Critics praise this rare Stoppard revival as an intellectually rich masterpiece, with David Greenspan delivering a brilliant performance. The dense, language-driven work offers exceptional ideas and signature humor that reward engaged audiences.
